B-REPLICATE-BAYESIAN-NULL.description: Parent shuffled-action null for Bayesian model comparison
B-REPLICATE-BAYESIAN-NULL.observed: null centered POSITIVE (~+3700 to +4000 nats), Occam's razor FAILS

observations: ALL three tested alpha_prior values (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) have shuffled-action null MEDIAN >= 0 nats (positive, range +3621 to +4048 nats). Occam's razor FAILS to penalize the larger model under the null.
The null distribution is centered at approximately +3700 to +4000 nats, NOT negative as required for valid Bayesian model comparison.

The observed log Bayes factors on the stochastic SPA are large positive values (+4665 to +5365 nats for K2), but they are NOT significantly above the null distribution (p=0.002 for all alpha_priors, which is > 0.001 threshold).
The deterministic SPA positive control shows even larger log Bayes factors (+5006 to +5699 nats for K2), confirming the implementation detects strong action effects.

K3 (action history) produces larger log Bayes factors than K2 (state history) by 419-592 nats, suggesting action history provides additional information. However, this comparison is not statistically tested because C1 fails.

The Dirichlet-Multinomial marginal likelihood has systematic upward bias under the null: when actions are shuffled, the full model M1 still achieves higher marginal likelihood than the reduced model M0.
This is the 5th estimator family tested on this SPA class: plug-in KL (FALSIFIED), entropy-rate CMI (FALSIFIED), KSG CMI (insensitive), LR chi2 (history collapse), and now Bayesian (FALSIFIED).
validity_notes: The Dirichlet-Multinomial marginal likelihood operates on a DIFFERENT scale than CMI (nats vs bits). The decision criteria were adapted: C1 uses null median < 0 nats instead of |null_mean| < 0.1 bits.

The null centering failure is NOT a Laplace smoothing bias (the Bayesian approach does NOT use histogram smoothing). It is a fundamental property of the Dirichlet-Multinomial marginal likelihood under this SPA design.
The null distribution has small standard deviation (36-44 nats) relative to the mean (~3700-4000 nats), indicating the upward bias is consistent and not due to variance.
N=5000 transitions (50 sessions x 100 steps) with seed=42, same as parent experiments.
Stratum coverage: 1438 K2 strata, 841 K3 strata. Most strata are small (5-9 records: 343 strata, 10-19 records: 37 strata). No strata have 20+ records.
unresolved: Why does the Dirichlet-Multinomial marginal likelihood have systematic upward bias under the null? The Dirichlet-Multinomial should penalize model complexity through marginalization over parameters, but it does not in this case.
Is the upward bias intrinsic to the Dirichlet-Multinomial family, or is it specific to this SPA design with many small strata?
Would alternative Bayesian model comparison methods (e.g., WAIC, LOO-CV, fractional Bayes factors) achieve valid null centering?
Can the K3-K2 difference (419-592 nats) be tested as evidence for beyond-Markov dynamics using a different null framework?
